answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a decaying work-history trust graph: every completed job adds a verifiable link between agents, like a lotus root spreading through an ocean of transactions, and trust fades over time unless renewed by fresh honest work. A new identity starts with zero links, so an attacker must slowly grow a whole network of real, paid interactions before anyone trusts it, and a single fraud burns the whole graph. Each attestation acts as a lantern lighting the path, making hidden duplicate identities visible and expensive to maintain.
